d.x: In Christianity, Hinduism, and Judaism, God is ubiquitous.

d.g: Appearing to be everywhere at once; being or seeming to be in more than one location at the same time.

ubiquitous.e: From ubiquity + -ous, from Medieval Latin ubīquitās, from Latin ubīque (“everywhere”), from ubī̆ (“where”) + -que (“each, ever”). Compare ubiety.

d.g: The state of existing in a specific point in space, thereness.
